title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: When a Reactivation Date Exists
content:
Under the reactivation policy for Savings & Money Market Accounts products brought back by the customer's own transfer out, the reactivation date is an all-or-nothing figure. This page states how the account's status and the tests on the dating transfer combine into that figure.

## Rule

- **Status comes into it.** Only an account whose status is dormant is reactivated. For an active, applied or closed account the policy yields no date and nothing is recorded, whatever the ledger holds.
- **Every test must pass at once.** For a dormant account, the date is the posting date of the dating transfer if, and only if, that transfer satisfies every test the policy sets for it. A single failed test leaves no date at all.
- **No substitute date.** Where no date is established, the policy does not fall back on some other entry, an earlier transfer or the day of the contact. It simply yields no reactivation date.

## Truth table (hypothetical accounts)

| Account status | Dating transfer passes all of the policy's tests | Reactivation date |
|---|---|---|
| dormant | yes | the transfer's posting date |
| dormant | no | none |
| active | yes | none, the account is not dormant |
| active | no | none |

## Points of judgement

**The account was already active when the customer called. Is a reactivation recorded anyway, to refresh the activity date?** No. Reactivation applies only to a dormant account.

**One test fails but the others pass. Is a partial or provisional date recorded?** No. The outcome is either a date or nothing.
